steps.text: Place strawberries in a blender; purée until smooth.
Transfer strawberry purée to a saucepan over medium heat; bring to a boil, stirring often, until reduced by at least half, about 20 minutes. Remove from heat and cool completely.

Beat butter with an electric mixer in a bowl until light and fluffy. Beat in 1 cup confectioners' sugar until combined. Beat 2 tablespoons cooled strawberry purée and vanilla extract into butter mixture until just blended.
Beat in 1 cup confectioners' sugar until combined, followed by 2 tablespoons strawberry purée. Repeat this step once more.
Beat remaining 1/2 cup confectioners' sugar into mixture until just blended.

raw_recipe.headline: Real Strawberry Frosting
raw_recipe.description: This strawberry frosting uses 4 simple ingredients, including fresh strawberries, for a gorgeous-colored, naturally flavored icing with no gelatin.

review.reviewBody: I really wanted that strawberry flavor to shine--what I did was add one teaspoon of strawberry extract and add an additional teaspoon of confectioners' sugar to make up for the additional liquid. I also added a dash of salt because Grandma taught me to always do so when making homemade frosting. This was FANTASTIC. It turned out like bakery frosting and the family kept eating the frosting off the cake.........and leaving the cake!

This strawberry frosting was the star of my strawberry cake. Better than the cake part, itself. It had a very wonderful clear fresh strawberry flavor. Honestly, I was surprised how lovely the flavor and color was! Like one commenter, I used almond extract instead of vanilla, because I love almond extract. The almond only accentuated the strawberry flavor. It didn't overwhelm it.

I prefer weight measurements for some ingredients. Since "1 cup of strawberries" is a slightly ambiguous amount, I can say that from the success of my icing, I'd recommend using about 250 grams (8.8 or even 9 oz) of hulled strawberries to make the full batch of the puree. I didn't exactly time the simmering time, but I did reduce by at least half. It was pretty deep red when it was done, which gave the icing the lovely color.

I used sifted Swerve confectioner's sugar substitute in place of regular confectioner's sugar to keep the sugar grams down. I used slightly less Swerve (that is supposed to measure 1:1 with regular confectioner's) than the recipe called for. I'm sure with regular confectioner's sugar the frosting is equally if not even yummier, if that is even possible. One might want to taste with a little less confectioner's sugar. Nicely ripe strawberries may or may not necessitate the additional sweetness, as long as the spreadability is just right.

The photo of my cake, attached, is of a small 6" single layer cake. [I made a few.]

I picked this recipe as my 3 yr-old grandson wanted pink icing and I didn't want to use red food color. I loved the fresh strawberry flavor of this icing. I did start out with 2 cups chopped strawberries. After puree step I had 1 cup. I cooked the puree about 20 minutes, strained it in and sieve, and ended up with slightly over 1/2 cup puree. Although the recipe asked for about 6 Tb. puree, I ended up using almost all the puree. I only added 3 cups total confectioner's sugar. It was really really good.

Real Strawberry Frosting by Candice. Yummy, but thin so I added an 8oz block cream cheese = strawberry ice cream flavored frosting! :) 'Syrupy so folded in two cups whipped cream (1c before whipping). Less strawberry flavor, of course, but it kept its shape well enough to frost cupcakes. I don't know that there is a "problem" with this recipe, but maybe less butter would help the lack of firmness - & not add cream cheese or whipped cream. Very good recipe, it was a bit too sweet for the test batch so I added 4 Cherry Tomatoes to the main recipe. After blending and straining the strawberry/tomato puree, it's way better! You can't taste the tomatoes, and the strawberry flavor is more strawberry-ey. Also I used half salted butter and half unsalted butter for the flavor, and a teaspoon of cream of tartar to make the frosting whip better.

This was amazing. I follow the advice of another reviewer and added about a half to a cup more of strawberries to purée and a pinch of salt. I also added a teaspoon of strawberry extract for a little extra oomph. I cooked the purée a little longer to make it a bit more concentrated. It came together beautifully. I used it between layers of a strawberry sponge cake that had chocolate ganache topping, and everyone raves about how delicious it was. I had a little extra left over and set it out in case anyone wanted extra, and it went fast! Great recipe.

This was very yummy. I used the recipe as inspiration for the creative process. I made this is January so my strawberries were frozen, while I was boiling down the puree, I added some purple liquid from a jar of beets (not the vinegar kind, just water) this gave the color vibrance and depth. I added a few more tb of beet liquid while I was beating the sugar and butter. The color was really pretty while still all natural. I wanted a bit more creamy texture (I used it for frosting and piping) so I added a splash of milk. I also subbed a wee bit of almond extract for the vanilla. I definitely used more than 3.5 c sugar as I needed enough to frost, pipe borders and write a birthday message. The result was a beautiful hue of pink monochrome that tasted wonderful. There was no taste of beet or almond, just a mellow strawberry flavor that wasnt overly sweet. Everyone who ate it commented on how good the frosting was. What I really liked about this frosting is that its all butter no shortening. I had made a vanilla yellow squash cake that I froze (I always frost my cakes frozen, the frosting was smooth enough to pipe beautifully then the butter hardened up on the cold cake to really set up perfect I was able to put saran wrap right on it once it was done without worry that the frosting would stick or be ruined. I want to try it with other fruits in the summer.

I have to rate it a 4 because I did modify it a bit, but it's AMAZING!!! I'm so happy I found the recipe on a whim and decided to try it. I am not a huge fan of strawberry frosting, but I made lemon cupcakes and it went perfect with them. I used 1 2/3 cup sugar vs. the 2 1/2. It doesn't need any additional sugar in our opinions. I also didn't puree the fruit when it was done-I just used a potato masher in the pan while cooking the berries. :D

The strawberry flavour is good. I made it with half cream cheese and half butter, seeing that one comment had read that the butter was too strong. Great idea and the icing was so smooth and beautiful. Just the nicest summer flavours.

I absolutely loved this recipe. I hate artificial strawberry flavor and wanted something without it... Thats how I landed on this recipe. One tip I've figured out is to make it a few days prior to using it, as the strawberries become even sweeter and more flavorful when they sit in the fridge all mixed up. Just dont forget if you do this, you will need to bring it out to room temperature before frosting with it.

Delicious! I used 1 1/2 cups of frozen strawberries and thawed them overnight in the refrigerator. After blending them smooth, I reduced them on the stove for at least 30 minutes. I put in 1/2 teaspoon vanilla extract and 1/2 teaspoon almond extract instead of the full teaspoon of vanilla, and I included a pinch of salt. I did put in the final 1/2 cup of powdered sugar. This recipe was just barely enough for one dozen cupcakes. I might make more next time to ensure I have enough. 

Great recipe! I used this buttercream to top white chocolate-vanilla cupcakes for my daughter’s first birthday!

I was happily shocked at just how "Strawberry" this is. Mine wasn't as dark colored as pictured, but was pink. Honestly, who cares? It's delicious, spreads like a dream, and keeps It's shape well. It was a little on the sweet side, but I'll just cut back on the sugar next time. Thank you for sharing, Candice!
I liked this recipe for it's lightness and creamy texture. The color was a light pink. It had a unique flavor and not too sweet.
Very good! Applied this puree in between layers of the strawberry cake from scratch.
AMAZING!!! I’ve made this ever so times now and it’s a hit! The flavor is so rich and delicious. Everyone has loved it

absolutely wonderful! I'd been looking for a good strawberry frosting recipe and this is it. The flavor blooms overnight. I'm going to try this with different berries. I think the puree would be a good addition to smoothies.
Surprisingly delicious. Next time I will let the butter get more room temperature ahead of making this to get the icing more fluffy. I am going to try to freeze some of it - its so good!
it was soooooooooooooooooo good😍

To me it tasted like cotton candy icing. It seems I started with less than 2 cups of strawberries (I doubled the recipe) and after cooking it down it concerned me that I may have too little. Thank LORD JESUS though it worked out perfectly, to me. Thank you for making this recipe available! My wife enjoyed it too, who is a self-proclaimed cake expert!
Love this frosting! But do I need to refrigerate the frosted cake?
